answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making every new identity dock at a public jetty of time-locked stake before it can vote or grade. That bond sits in a visible lagoon of vesting funds, slashable if the same operator is caught spinning clones. When an identity's attested-work score hits a nadir—too few independent countersignatures versus its claims—peers refuse to mine its transactions, so cheap replica swarms never accumulate settlement weight.
